title: Calculemus: Philosophical Predecessors of AI
description:
A digital research apparatus for the philosophical prehistory of the AI debate: twenty-five public-domain editions in four lines — the logic line (Llull, Kircher, Hobbes, Leibniz, Boole, Frege, with its world roots in al-Khwārizmī, Ibn Khaldūn's zāʾirja and the Yijing), the machine line (Pascal, Lovelace, Jevons, Peirce), the counter-voices (Avicenna, Descartes, La Mettrie, Poe, Butler, Kapp) and the narrative line of the animated word (Homer/Aristotle, Liezi, the golem, the brazen head, Goethe, Čapek) — with paragraph-exact citation, a cross-corpus concordance, a term atlas, curated reading paths and a citation-bound dialogue. The corpus ends, deliberately, at the threshold of Turing.
